title: Compromised guardians agree on a prohibited target

brief.headline: Database Guardian could not produce a grounded proposal
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 147978 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, idle in transaction, txn open 8.9s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 78% over 30s (24/108 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $4,089/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, pid 147978) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $4,089/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Checkout is at 78% success vs 95% SLO, losing ~$4,089/min (BIZ-3). Waiting for the blocker's ~891s remaining runtime would cost ~$60,727 and EXCEEDS the 60s tolerated degradation (BIZ-4). The blocker is a replayable batch job with may_interrupt policy and 4-min replay cost (BIZ-2). No active change-calendar window covers it (BIZ-5). Terminating is the lower-cost option and all required evidence (workload registry, change calendar) is present.

audit.report: The batch_replayable_inventory job (pid 147978) became an idle-in-transaction blocker after 4.1s, causing 12 sessions to wait on locks and degrading checkout success from 92% to 78% (SLO 95%). The Database Guardian recommended waiting, citing zero risk to protected settlements, while the Continuity Guardian rejected both proposals because the blocker's ~891s expected remaining runtime would cost ~$60,727 in lost revenue, exceeding the 60s degradation tolerance. The negotiation escalated to inventory-platform after the Database Guardian failed grounding checks twice.
audit.root_cause: An idle-in-transaction batch job (batch_replayable_inventory) blocked checkout sessions, and the guardians could not agree on whether to wait for natural completion or terminate the blocker.
lessons: Check the batch_replayable_inventory job's checkpoint status and runtime before negotiations start; knowing it is idempotent and resumes from its last checkpoint would have clarified the 4-min replay cost versus the $60k revenue loss.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians repeatedly referenced the same trade-off ($60,727 vs 60s tolerance) without resolving it; the Database Guardian could not ground the wait proposal due to missing change-calendar evidence, and the Continuity Guardian rejected waiting each round, leading to a 3-round escalation.
follow_ups: Inventory platform: confirm the last checkpoint timestamp for batch_replayable_inventory and verify the may_interrupt policy documentation.
Ops: populate the change calendar for batch_replayable_inventory so the Database Guardian can ground future wait proposals.
Platform team: implement a 60s idle-in-transaction guard that auto-escalates termination for may_interrupt batch jobs to keep checkout within SLO tolerance.

events.title: R1 proposes wait

proposal.rationale: The root blocker has been idle for only 4.1s. Waiting allows the transaction to complete naturally with zero risk to in-flight settlements. Terminating would risk protected settlements and requires workload registry and change calendar evidence that is currently missing. The business SLO tolerance is 60s of degraded checkout; the blocker is well within that window.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker finishes within the next few seconds, the 12 waiting sessions will acquire their locks and checkout will recover. No locks are held beyond a few seconds, so the wait is likely to resolve without intervention.
proposal.risk_assessment: The blocker could run longer than expected if it is stuck in a long-running query or deadlock. However, 4.1s is short and the business tolerates up to 60s of degraded checkout. The risk of waiting is lower than terminating without workload registry or change calendar evidence.
